players.name: Travis Head
players.didyouKnow: In 2015, Head was named captain of the Redbacks and at the age of 21 became the state's youngest captain of all time.
players.bio:
A former Hampshire scholar and Australia Under-19 representative, left-handed batter Travis Head had a golden run of form at the start of the 2013-14 season that led South Australia coach Darren Berry to describe him as a future Test player.

Alongside his batting prowess, Head was long touted as a leader-in-the-making when he led South Australia to their Under-19 National Championship title in 2012-13. His leadership skills were clearly admired as, at the remarkable age of 21, he was named the youngest captain of his state team.

In and out of the nation's Test and ODI sides across the first five years of his international career, Head cemented his spot as one of Australia's most important batters with an incredible 148-ball 152 at the Gabba in the opening Test of the 2021-22 Ashes.

He was awarded player of the match for his 163 in Australia's maiden World Test Championship triumph against India in 2023, and seized his chance as Aaron Finch's replacement to open the batting in the ODI side after his retirement in 2022.

Despite suffering a broken hand a few weeks out from the 2023 50-over World Cup in India, Head was deemed that important to Australia's chances that selectors opted to carry him through the first half of the tournament.

He duly delivered with a stunning 59-ball hundred in his first match of the tournament against New Zealand in Dharamsala, and finished the campaign with another player-of-the-match performance in the final as his 137 against India sealed a remarkable sixth ODI World Cup for the country.

Head has also had an illustrious career in the Big Bash League with the Adelaide Strikers, recording the club's first ever century along with leading them to their championship title in BBL|07, but it took until the 2023-24 summer for his to establish himself as a three-format player for Australia.

He won his first Allan Border Medal at the 2025 Australian Cricket Awards, presented the prize in the lobby of the Sri Lanka hotel where the Australian Test team was on tour.

An injury to Usman Khawaja saw Head make a surprise elevation to open the batting in the opening Test of the 2025-26 Ashes, and responded by peeling off an incredible 123 from just 83 balls. He remained as Test opener for the rest of the series, hitting two further centuries - in Adelaide and Sydney - and finishing the series with 629 runs at 62.90.

players.name: Mitch Marsh
players.didyouKnow: Marsh became the youngest player to debut in Australian domestic one-day cricket when he played for Western Australia at the age of 17 i
players.bio:
Having chosen cricket over a career as an Australian Rules footballer, Mitchell Marsh wasted no time showing off the natural ability that he shares with his Test-playing father Geoff and brother Shaun.

He made his state debut at the age of 17, was an Under-19 World Cup-winning captain at 18 and earned an international call-up at 19.

Having opted against the big money on offer in the Indian Premier League in 2014, Marsh burst back onto the scene with a double-century for Australia A against India A.

Later that year he earned a Test debut, against Pakistan in Dubai, and while the allrounder's career in the longest format has struggled to garner long-term continuity, he has certainly saved his best performances for England in the Ashes. This includes two centuries in the 2017-18 home series, and figures of 5-46 at The Oval in 2019.

He then made a triumphant return to the Test team midway through the 2023 Ashes with a barnstorming century at Headingley in his first Test innings in almost four years. An excellent ODI World Cup and home summer against Pakistan and the West Indies followed, which saw the right-hander win his first Allan Border Medal.

Marsh also established himself as a crucial member of Australia's white-ball sides. In the 2021 T20 World Cup, Marsh scored an important half-century in the team's final group stage clash against the West Indies before hammering 77 not out off just 50 balls against New Zealand in the final to be crowned player of the match as Australia lifted their maiden World Cup in the format.

He captained Australia's T20 side for the first time in South Africa in 2023, also leading the nation in the 50-over format during that white-ball series that followed with Pat Cummins out injured, and became the permanent T20I captain in May 2024 ahead of that year's T20 World Cup.

players.name: Cameron Green
players.bio:
Cameron Green had no shortage of hype to live up to in the early stages of his career having been touted as an international-calibre player since his early teens.

The towering allrounder, who stands nearly two metres tall, burst onto the first-class scene as a 17-year-old in February 2017 when he took a five-wicket haul against Tasmania in his first Sheffield Shield appearance with Western Australia.

His first 30 first-class wickets came at an average of just 22.53 but as stress fractures in his back limited his bowling in the ensuing years, it was the strides he made with the bat that vaulted him into national calculations.

Green's breakout game came in November 2019 when he hit unbeaten scores of 87 and 121 from No.8 and 9 against Queensland, which saw him promoted up the WA order and subsequently flourish as a top-order player with two more centuries in the season, before 197 off 438 against NSW in October 2020.

A mainstay in WA's top four and having resumed bowling following months of remedial work on his action, he earned a call-up to Australian squads in late 2020, making his ODI and Test debut that summer against India.

He passed fifty in five of his first six series, took a maiden five-wicket haul at the MCG against South Africa in the 2022 Boxing Day Test, and hit his first Test century against India in Ahmedabad in March 2023, all while building a stunning highlight reel of remarkable catches in the gully.

Opening the batting on a T20I tour of India in September 2022 proved life-changing, flaying a pair of impressive fifties that led to him being bought for a then-record A$3.15million by Mumbai Indians in that year's IPL auction, and rewarded his purchasers with a 47-ball century that elevated them into the playoffs.

A hamstring issue in the 2023 Ashes saw him lose his spot to fellow WA allrounder Mitch Marsh but, so eager were selectors to get him back into the side, Steve Smith was moved up to open the batting in the wake of David Warner's Test retirement to accommodate Green at No. 4. He struck a masterful unbeaten 174 not out in his new role against New Zealand in Wellington in February 2024.

After developing a stress fracture in his back in mid-2024 Green opted for surgery that ruled him out for that summer's Border-Gavaskar Trophy series and restricted him from bowling until late in 2025. He returned as a batter only via the UK's County Championship in mid-2025 playing as a No.3. After building up bowling loads in the Sheffield Shield, Green was shown the confidence to be named as an allrounder in Australia's squad for the opening Ashes Test that summer.

players.name: Tim David
players.bio:
Big-hitting Tim David has forged a path like no other in Australian cricket.

Born in Singapore and raised in Perth, in his younger years David struggled to make an impact at state level and, despite landing a Big Bash contract, similarly struggled for regular matches with the Perth Scorchers.

Dedicating his career to the 20-over format, in 2019 he opted to play for his country of birth and, soon after, things began to rapidly change for the ‘finisher’. Signed by the Hobart Hurricanes for the 2020-21 season, David flourished in the Apple Isle and soon found himself playing for Lahore Qalandars in the Pakistan Super League.

Success followed there and subsequently in the UK, further boosting his profile. In early 2022, David landed a mammoth AUD$1.5 million IPL deal with Mumbai Indians. The step up didn’t faze him; in fact he thrived, finishing the tournament with the highest ever strike-rate (216.27) from a player to have faced a minimum of 50 balls.

In September 2022 David made his debut for Australia (under ICC eligibility rules) against India in Mohali and, in just his third match, smashed 54 off 27 in Hyderabad.

players.name: Josh Inglis
players.bio:
England-born but WA-bred, Josh Inglis made his first-class debut for the Cricket Australia XI in 2015 in a tour match against West Indies.

The versatile wicketkeeper-batter was rewarded with a Western Australia contract at the beginning of the 2016-17 season, but it wasn't until the 2019-20 summer that Inglis started to really make his mark.

That Big Bash campaign the right-hander finished with 405 runs (just 20 runs behind Scorchers' leading run-scorer Liam Livingstone), including four half-centuries.

The next year, in BBL|10, he exceeded the 400-run barrier again and followed up with some impressive performances for London Spirit in the inaugural season of The Hundred.

By this stage, Inglis was firmly in the eyes of the Australian selectors and in February 2022 he made his international debut in a home T20 against Sri Lanka before an ODI debut – this time away to Sri Lanka – followed in June of the same year.

At the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, for which Inglis was selected as the squad's reserve keeper, he replaced Alex Carey in the XI after one match and held his spot throughout for Australia's famous victory in Ahmedabad.

During Australia's tour of the United Kingdom in 2024, Inglis set a new Australian record with a 43-ball T20 century against Scotland.

He became Australia's 30th ODI captain, and the 14th in T20 internationals, when named to lead in home series against Pakistan in 2024-25, while his hot form also earned him a maiden call up to the Test squad as a specialist batter for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy series.

He made his Test debut against Sri Lanka in Galle in late January 2025, scoring a century on debut, making him only the fourth Australian man to score centuries in all three formats of the game.

players.name: Glenn Maxwell
players.didyouKnow: Maxwell learned to bat left-handed while at primary school because nobody could dismiss him when he batted right-handed and he was told he would be ba
players.bio:
One of the world's most dynamic and exciting players, Victorian Glenn Maxwell has revolutionised one-day and T20 batting.

The allrounder first gained global fame in 2013 when, just six months after his international debut, he earned a million-dollar contract from Indian Premier League franchise Mumbai Indians.

He first showed promising signs for Australia in white-ball cricket during the side's ODI tour of India in late 2013, scoring 172 of his 248 runs in boundaries. A few months later, Maxwell justified his IPL hype with a successful season with Kings XI Punjab – also finishing as the league's third-highest run-scorer.

Maxwell also made his Test debut that year but by late 2022 had played just seven Tests – all in Asia – the highlight of which was a maiden century in 2017 against India in Ranchi.

In his side's triumphant 2015 ODI World Cup campaign, the Victorian smashed a 51-ball ton against Sri Lanka at the SCG – the quickest for Australia in ODIs. He broke his own record against the Netherlands in the tournament's 2023 edition by reaching three figures in 40 balls, which was also the fastest World Cup century. No Australian has more T20 international hundreds (five) than Maxwell, which puts him level with India captain Rohit Sharma.

A crowd-favourite in the Big Bash League, in early 2022 Maxwell smashed an incredible 154 not out against the Hobart Hurricanes, becoming the first ever player to pass 150 in the competition. The clash at the MCG was also Maxwell’s 100th BBL match, becoming just the sixth player to reach the milestone.

But perhaps his finest moment came during the 2023 ODI World Cup triumph when he became the first Australian man to score an international double-century in the 50-over format, with his incredible unbeaten 201 while suffering severe cramps single-handedly lifting his side from 7-91 to chase down Afghanistan's 5-291.

players.name: Matt Renshaw
players.didyouKnow: In December 2018, Renshaw scored 345 for Toombul off 273 balls, with 38 fours and 12 sixes, a record for Brisbane senior cricket.
players.bio:
An Under-19 representative for Australia, Renshaw burst onto the domestic scene in December 2015 when struck an epic 170 against a strong NSW attack to become the youngest first-class century maker for Queensland. Born in Yorkshire, he was a family friend of England batter Joe Root as a youngster.

After his mammoth breakout innings, Renshaw finished his maiden Sheffield Shield campaign as Queensland's leading Shield run scorer with 738 at 43.41 in 2015-16.

In 2017, Renshaw became the first Australian cricketer to make 500 Test runs before turning 21 years old which included a memorable 184 against Pakistan in Sydney.

However, following his dream start a difficult six Tests in Asia (four in India, two in Bangladesh) and a barren start to the following Shield season saw Renshaw left out of the Aussie team for the 2017-18 Ashes series, with Cameron Bancroft preferred.

Ironically, it was Renshaw who was called up to replace the suspended Bancroft during the ill-fated tour of South Africa in early 2018.

A couple of lean seasons saw Renshaw move to the middle order, where he flourished during the Covid-affected 2020-21 summer, scoring 500 Shield runs at an average of 62.50. His one-day and T20 form also improved following his positional shift.

A strong county campaign with Somerset in 2022 followed and ahead of the 2022-23 New Year's Test against South Africa, Renshaw was recalled to the Australian XI.

The tall left-hander also played two Tests on Australia's unsuccessful tour to India in 2023.

Two centuries for Australia A as opener saw him return to the top of the order for the 2023-24 Marsh Sheffield Shield season and 2024 County Championship season.

players.name: Marcus Stoinis
players.didyouKnow: In May 2016, Stoinis achieved his career best T20 figures against the Mumbai Indians, returning 4-15 for Kings XI Punjab.
players.bio:
Debuting for his home state of Western Australia as a 19-year-old, Marcus Stoinis eventually moved to Victoria in 2012 seeking more opportunities as a young cricketer.

The allrounder didn’t take long to make his mark in the Sheffield Shield, with a breathtaking 170 against Tasmania in the 2013-14 season, followed by topping the run-scorers’ list for his state in 2014-15.

Within a year, Stoinis made his ODI & T20I debuts before being left out for nearly a year and a half from both formats.

However his consistent performances in first-class cricket earned him an ODI recall; a career-defining comeback which saw him smash 146 not out and claim three wickets against New Zealand. While his efforts didn’t get his side get over the finish line, it did manage to seal his spot in Australia’s limited over formats.

Named Australia’s ODI cricketer of the year in 2018-19, Stoinis has also been hugely impressive as a Melbourne Stars player the Big Bash League, with his then Big Bash record score of 147 off 79 balls a standout performance in BBL|09.

Stoinis was a key part of Australia’s maiden T20 World Cup triumph in 2021, guiding the team home (alongside Matthew Wade) in the first group stage match of the tournament against South Africa, and a nail-biting semi-final win over Pakistan.

players.name: Xavier Bartlett
players.bio:
A strong fast bowler from the Gold Coast, Xavier Bartlett's ability to swing the new ball both ways at pace makes him a potent threat at the start of the innings in all three formats.

Born in Adelaide, Bartlett's family moved to Queensland when he was a child. He came through the age-groups ranks with Queensland and made his first XI Premier Cricket debut for Gold Coast Dolphins as a 17-year-old.

The right-armer represented Australia at the 2018 Under-19 World Cup before making his one-day debut for the Bulls later that year, before getting his first taste of the Sheffield Shield at the beginning of the 2019-20 season.

Barlett initially made an impression for the Brisbane Heat in KFC BBL|10 in one-over bursts under the 'X-factor' rule in place for that season, but it wasn't long before he became a mainstay for the teal team.

After playing an important role in the Heat's unlikely run to the BBL|12 final, he was the leading wicket-taker the following season as he helped Brisbane go one better and take out the title.

Bartlett made his international debut on the back of that outstanding tournament, shining in his first match for Australia in an ODI at the MCG after taking a wicket with just his third delivery.

players.name: Nathan Ellis
players.bio:
From a labourer struggling to make ends meet to an international cricketer, the journey of Nathan Ellis is one of extraordinary dedication and persistence.

Raised in Sydney, Ellis relocated to Hobart in 2017 in search of an opportunity at the next level having dominated NSW Premier Cricket by taking 160 wickets at 22 in four seasons.

A consistent contributor for the Hobart Hurricanes since his debut in 2018, the right-armer quickly became one of the competition's best death bowlers with twin weapons of an excellent change of pace and pinpoint yorkers.

On the shorter side for a quick, making his deliveries skid on, he has earned multiple stints in overseas T20 leagues where he has impressed for Hampshire (T20 Blast), London Spirit (Hundred) and Punjab Kings (IPL).

He made an instant impact on T20 international debut for Australia with a hat-trick against Bangladesh in 2021, also earning an ODI cap in Pakistan in 2022. With opportunities to represent Australia limited behind a generational pool of talent, Ellis initially had to bide his time, called up for his first World Cup role at the 2024 T20 event in the Caribbean.

While he has also enjoyed success with the red-ball at first-class level after making his debut for Tasmania in 2020, his overseas and international opportunities have come exclusively in the white-ball formats, helping him earn a Cricket Australia contract for 2024-25 after being upgraded during the previous season.

Ellis was appointed Hurricanes captain ahead of BBL|13, replacing Matthew Wade, and captained the side to the BBL|14 title in January 2025.

players.name: Adam Zampa
players.didyouKnow: Zampa was the leading wicket-taker for Australia in the 2016 ICC World Twenty20 hosted by India.
players.bio:
A leg-spinner from New South Wales' south coast, Adam Zampa showed early signs of his ability after playing an instrumental role in Australia's successful campaign at the 2010 Under-19 World Cup.

Following his impressive performances for South Australia and the Melbourne Stars, the wily spinner made his way into Australia's ODI and T20I squads in 2016. Zampa emerged as Australia's leading wicket-taker at the T20 World Cup hosted by India the same year.

By 2019 Zampa had established himself as one of the first picked bowlers in Australia's ODI and T20 setups, and an impressive career trajectory has seemingly seen him improve year-on-year.

Typifying the modern white-ball wrist spinner with a skidding stock delivery, Zampa proved crucial in Australia's maiden T20 World Cup triumph in the UAE in 2021.

He finished with 13 wickets at an economy rate of just 5.81 and was considered by several judges as unlucky not to be named Player of the Tournament.

He again played a vital role in Australia's 2023 ODI World Cup victory, overcoming a slow start to finish the tournament as the second highest wicket-taker with 23.

He became the first Australian bowler to play 100 T20 Internationals during the Carribean tour in mid-2025
